title: Tonno Sott'olio in Salsa alla Bolognese (Canned Tuna in Bolognese Sauce)
description: A sauce made with onion, garlic, and celery.

ingredients.name: White celery stalks (two, one palm long)
ingredients.sourceText: White celery stalks (two, one palm long)

steps: Put the canned tuna in boiling water and let it boil gently for half an hour, changing the water every ten minutes, for a total of three changes.
Meanwhile, make a finely chopped mixture with half a small onion, a quarter clove of garlic, two white celery stalks each one palm long, a good piece of carrot and an abundant handful of parsley.
Put it on heat with three tablespoons of oil and 15 grams of butter.
When it has taken color, stop it with two fingers of glass of water and let it boil briefly.
Once the tuna is cool, cut it into the thinnest slices you can.
In a pan, spread it in layers, alternating with the sauce and 15 grams of butter scattered in pieces.
Bring to a boil over heat to liquify the butter.
Squeeze half a lemon over it and serve hot.
This will be enough for four people as a first course at a meatless lunch or as an intermediate course at a family dinner.

title: Tordi Disossati in Gelatina (Boned Thrushes in Aspic)
description: Prepared with aspic, veal, and tongue.
steps: Set aside half of the tongue and one third of the prosciutto (more fat than lean), and mince and pound the veal together with the remaining tongue and prosciutto in a mortar with the truffle skin, softening the mixture with a drop of marsala.
Pass the mixture through a sieve and add one egg yolk.
Bone the thrushes as you would for stuffed chicken (Recipe No. 258), leaving the neck and head attached.
Fill them with the described mixture, to which you have already mixed the truffle, tongue, and prosciutto that were set aside, all cut into small cubes.
Sew them closed so that the thread can be removed when cooked.
Wrap each thrush in a piece of cheesecloth and boil for one hour in aspic broth (Recipe No. 3).
Serve as a cold dish on the same aspic, and if you form six molds shaped like nests with the aspic, it will appear that the thrush is sitting on top to brood.

title: Tordi finti (Mock Thrushes)
description: Prepared with veal, berries, and chicken.

ingredients.name: Lean veal without bone for six thrushes, 300 grams
ingredients.sourceText: Lean veal without bone for six thrushes, 300 grams

steps: Cut the veal into six thin slices and flatten them, shaping them nicely and setting aside the trimmings.
Mince together the trimmings, chicken livers, a piece of lard, the juniper berries, cleaned anchovies, and a sage leaf very finely, seasoning with a little salt and pepper to form the filling.

Roll the meat slices around this filling, then wrap each with a thin slice of lard, placing half a sage leaf between the lard and the meat, and tie in a cross pattern. About 60 grams of lard in total should suffice.
Heat three tablespoons of oil in a sauté pan or open pot over high heat, place the rolled meat inside and lightly season with salt and pepper.
When browned on all sides, drain off the fat, leaving the browned bits on the bottom of the pan, and finish cooking with broth added little by little so they remain almost dry at the end.
Serve untied over six slices of lightly toasted bread moistened with the concentrated pan sauce.
They are also good served cold.

title: Torta alla Marengo (Marengo Cake)
description: A cake made with cake, short crust, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: Short crust pastry, half the dose
ingredients.sourceText: Short crust pastry, half the dose

steps: Make a short crust pastry.
Make a cream with milk, sugar, flour, three egg yolks, and vanilla.
Take {{source-6}} and cut it into slices half a centimeter thick.

Use a medium-sized copper pan, butter it and cover the bottom with a sheet of the said pastry; then superimpose on this all around an edge of the same pastry one finger wide and two high, and to attach it well, wet the edge with a wet finger.
After making this frame for the pan, cover the bottom pastry with half of the sponge cake slices lightly dipped in cedar rosoli.
Over these spread the cream and cover this with the remaining sponge cake slices equally sprinkled with rosoli.

Now beat with a whisk two of the three remaining egg whites from the cream and when they are very firm add to them little by little 130 grams of powdered sugar and mix slowly to thus have the meringue with which you will cover the surface of the sweet, leaving uncovered the edge of the short pastry to gild it with egg yolk.
Bake it in the oven or country oven and when the meringue has hardened cover it with a sheet so it does not take color.
Turn the cake out cold and dust it lightly with powdered sugar.

title: Torta coi Pinoli (Cake with Pine Nuts)
description: A cake made with pine nuts, semolina, and white wine.
steps: The amount of semolina is not entirely strict, but make sure it comes out rather firm.
Chop the pine nuts with a pastry cutter to the thickness of half a grain of rice.
When the semolina is cooked in the milk add everything else and last the eggs mixing them quickly.
Make a short crust pastry with flour, butter, sugar, and one egg. If this is not enough to mix the flour, use a drop of white wine or Marsala.

Take a pan in which the sweet does not come higher than two fingers, butter it and cover the bottom with a thin sheet of the said pastry; pour the mixture into it and make the top with the same pastry.

title: Torta di Pane Bruno alla Tedesca (German-Style Dark Bread Cake)
description: A cake made with sweet almonds, cognac, and rye.

ingredients.name: Grated rye bread crust, 3 heaping spoonfuls
ingredients.sourceText: Grated rye bread crust, 3 heaping spoonfuls

ingredients.name: Powdered sugar and flour for dusting
ingredients.sourceText: Powdered sugar and flour for dusting

steps: First work the sugar with two of the whole eggs, then add the blanched and finely pounded almonds with one spoonful of the said sugar; work the mixture again, then add the breadcrumbs and three yolks, lastly the cognac
Whip the three remaining egg whites and fold them in
Prepare a proportioned baking pan, butter it and dust it with powdered sugar and flour
Bake it in the oven or in a country oven

Cover it with a tender crust like that of recipe 645, or with a chocolate coating made as follows: Put 30 grams of butter and 100 grams of chopped chocolate on the fire and when well melted add 30 grams of powdered sugar and spread the mixture on the cake when it is no longer boiling

title: Torta di Semolino (Semolina Cake)
description: A cake made with semolina, sweet almonds, and lemon.

ingredients.name: Sweet almonds with three bitter almonds, 100 grams
ingredients.sourceText: Sweet almonds with three bitter almonds, 100 grams

steps: Blanch the almonds in hot water and pound them very finely in a mortar with all the sugar, which you will add one spoonful at a time
Cook the semolina in the milk and before removing it from the fire add the butter and almonds, which, being mixed with the sugar, dissolve easily
Salt it and wait until it is lukewarm to add the eggs beaten separately
Pour the mixture into a buttered baking pan, sprinkled with breadcrumbs and of such size that the cake turns out one and a half fingers high or at most two
Bake it in the oven or in a country oven, unmold it when cold and serve it whole or cut into almond-shaped pieces

title: Torta Frangipane (Frangipane Cake)
description: A cake made with potato flour, powdered sugar, and butter.
steps: First work the egg yolks with the sugar, then add the potato flour and continue stirring with a spoon; then pour in the melted butter and finally the beaten egg whites and the powders.
Use a small pan so it remains two fingers high; butter it and dust it with flour mixed with sugar.
You can bake it at home in the country oven.

title: Torta Milanese (Milanese Cake)
description: A cake made with meat or beef or veal, chocolate, and pine nuts.

ingredients.name: Lean boiled or roasted meat of beef or veal, cleaned of sinews or tenderness, 200 grams
ingredients.sourceText: Lean boiled or roasted meat of beef or veal, cleaned of sinews or tenderness, 200 grams

ingredients.name: Candied citron cut into small pieces, 25 grams
ingredients.sourceText: Candied citron cut into small pieces, 25 grams

ingredients.name: White wine or marsala, as much as needed to blend it
ingredients.sourceText: White wine or marsala, as much as needed to blend it

steps: Chop the meat very finely with a mincing knife
Toast the pine nuts
Soak the raisins in marsala and dry them before use
Brown the meat in the butter, stirring continuously so it does not stick, and when it has taken on a somewhat reddish color, remove it from the fire to let it cool

Dissolve the chocolate, grated or in small pieces, over the fire in three spoonfuls of water, and when dissolved add the sugar and then pour it into the meat, adding the pine nuts, raisins and candied citron and mixing everything together
Now prepare a shortcrust pastry to enclose the cake

Take a proportionate baking pan where the mixture is no more than a finger high, grease it with butter or lard, and with one sheet below and another on top, the latter rolled out with a fluted roller, seal it between
Brush the surface with egg yolk, bake it in the oven or in a country oven and serve it cooled

title: Torta Ricciolina I (Curly Cake I)
description: A cake made with sweet almonds, powdered sugar, and fruit.

ingredients.name: Sweet almonds with some bitter ones, blanched, 120 grams
ingredients.sourceText: Sweet almonds with some bitter ones, blanched, 120 grams

steps: Mix two eggs with flour and make thin noodles equal to the finest ones you would cook for broth soup.

On one corner of the work surface make a mound with the almonds, sugar, candied fruit cut into pieces, and scraped lemon zest, and with a pastry cutter and rolling pin flatten and chop this pile of ingredients until it becomes as fine as grains of wheat.

Take a copper pan and without oiling it, begin to spread a layer of noodles in the middle, if it is large, and season them with the ingredients described above, spread another layer of noodles and season them again, repeating the operation until the ingredients are finished, making sure the cake comes out round and at least two fingers thick.
When it is thus prepared, pour the liquefied butter over it using a brush to oil it well on the surface and so the butter penetrates equally in all parts.
Bake it in the oven or in the country oven; in fact, to save coal, the lid of this alone may suffice.
Dust it abundantly with powdered sugar when it is hot and serve it cold.

title: Torta Ricciolina II (Curly Cake II)
description: A cake made with lard, sweet almonds, and candied orange.

ingredients.name: Sweet almonds with three bitter ones, blanched, 120 grams
ingredients.sourceText: Sweet almonds with three bitter ones, blanched, 120 grams

steps: Make a short crust pastry with flour, sugar, butter, lard, and one egg.

Spread one part to the thickness of a coin on the bottom of a copper pan 20 or 21 centimeters in diameter (first buttered) and over it pour a marzipan made with the following proportions: blanched sweet almonds with three bitter ones, sugar, butter, candied orange, one egg yolk.
Pound the almonds with sugar in the mortar, add the orange in small pieces, and with the butter, egg yolk and a spoonful of water make everything into a paste.
With the rest of the short crust pastry form a circle and with a wet finger attach it all around the edges of the pan.

Spread the marzipan evenly and cover it with a layer half a finger high of very thin noodles because these should be like a flowering, not the base of the sweet, and oil them with 20 grams of liquefied butter using a brush.
Bake the cake in the oven at moderate heat and after scatter over it 10 grams of candied citron in small pieces.
Dust it with vanilla-powdered sugar and serve it one or two days after cooking, because time softens it and makes it more delicate.
For the noodles make enough for one egg, but a little more than half will suffice.

title: Tortelli di Ceci (Chickpea Fritters)
description: Prepared with chickpeas, chestnuts, and fruit.

ingredients.name: Sapa, necessary amount to soften the mixture
ingredients.sourceText: Sapa, necessary amount to soften the mixture

ingredients.name: Mostarda di Savignano, half a small jar
ingredients.sourceText: Mostarda di Savignano, half a small jar

ingredients.name: Candied fruit, 40 grams in small pieces
ingredients.sourceText: Candied fruit, 40 grams in small pieces

ingredients.name: Sugar, a little if the sapa has not sweetened enough
ingredients.sourceText: Sugar, a little if the sapa has not sweetened enough

ingredients.name: White wine or marsala, about 3 spoonfuls
ingredients.sourceText: White wine or marsala, about 3 spoonfuls

steps: Soak the chickpeas overnight in fresh water.

In the morning unite with them 7 or 8 dried chestnuts and put them on the fire with equally fresh water in an earthenware pot with 3 grams of sodium carbonate tied in a small cloth (the people call this the secret and it serves to facilitate the cooking of chickpeas).

When they are cooked, remove them dry and pass them through a sieve while hot and boiling, together with the chestnuts; and if, despite the secret, they had remained hard due to the quality of the water, pound them in the mortar.

When you have passed them, season and flavor them with a pinch of salt, with sapa in the quantity necessary to make the mixture somewhat soft, half a small jar of mostarda di Savignano, 40 grams of candied fruit in small pieces, a little sugar if the sapa has not sweetened them enough, and two teaspoons of ground cinnamon.
For the dough: work together flour, butter, sugar, 1 egg, white wine or marsala, and a pinch of salt.
Draw out a sheet of dough about the thickness of half a coin and cut it with the scalloped round stamp.
Make the filling abundant in the discs and you will have, joining the edges, the tortelli in the form of a quarter moon.
Fry them in lard or oil and when they are no longer bubbling, dust them with powdered sugar.

sourceSteps: Soak the chickpeas overnight in fresh water.

In the morning unite with them 7 or 8 dried chestnuts and put them on the fire with equally fresh water in an earthenware pot with 3 grams of sodium carbonate tied in a small cloth (the people call this the secret and it serves to facilitate the cooking of chickpeas).

When they are cooked, remove them dry and pass them through a sieve while hot and boiling, together with the chestnuts; and if, despite the secret, they had remained hard due to the quality of the water, pound them in the mortar.

When you have passed them, season and flavor them with a pinch of salt, with sapa in the quantity necessary to make the mixture somewhat soft, half a small jar of mostarda di Savignano, 40 grams of candied fruit in small pieces, a little sugar if the sapa has not sweetened them enough, and two teaspoons of ground cinnamon.
For the dough: work together flour, butter, sugar, 1 egg, white wine or marsala, and a pinch of salt.
Draw out a sheet of dough about the thickness of half a coin and cut it with the scalloped round stamp.
Make the filling abundant in the discs and you will have, joining the edges, the tortelli in the form of a quarter moon.
Fry them in lard or oil and when they are no longer bubbling, dust them with powdered sugar.

With this amount you will make just under 300, and you will need a pasta sheet made with three eggs.

title: Tortellini di carne di piccione (Pigeon Meat Tortellini)
description: Prepared with pigeon, parmesan cheese, and nutmeg.

ingredients.name: One young pigeon, plucked, weighing approximately half a kilogram
ingredients.sourceText: One young pigeon, plucked, weighing approximately half a kilogram

steps: Empty the pigeon of its organs, as the liver and gizzard are not used in this case, and boil it.
To boil it, throw it into boiling water and salt it; half an hour of boiling is sufficient, as it should be undercooked.

Remove it from the heat, bone it, then mince very finely both this meat and the prosciutto first with a knife then with a lunette, and finally, adding the Parmesan and nutmeg, work the mixture with the blade of the knife to make it all homogeneous.
Use the stamp N. 8 to close them, and with three eggs of pasta you will obtain approximately 260.
You may serve them in broth, as a soup course, or dry dressed with cheese and butter, or better with sauce and giblets.

title: Tortino di Petonciani (Eggplant Cake)
description: A cake made with eggplants, parmesan cheese, and tomato sauce.
steps: Peel seven or eight eggplants, cut them into round slices and salt them so they release their water.
After a few hours, flour them and fry them in oil.
Take a pan that can withstand fire and, layer by layer, season them with grated Parmesan and tomato sauce N. 125, arranging them so they form a nice mound.
Beat an egg with a pinch of salt, a spoonful of said sauce, a teaspoon of Parmesan, two of breadcrumbs, and cover the surface with this mixture.
Place the pan under the lid of the country oven, with fire on top, and when the egg has set, serve the cake to the table.
It can be served alone, as an intermediate course or accompanied by a meat dish.

title: Trippa alla Corsa (Corsican Tripe)
description: Prepared with tripe, beef, and lard.
steps: Wash the tripe well and cut into strips no wider than half a finger, and cut the foot the same way
Mince the onion finely and place on heat with butter
When it begins to take color, add the finely chopped lard with the crescent-shaped chopping tool together with the garlic
When this soffritto has taken on a hazelnut color, add the tripe and foot, seasoning with salt, pepper and the indicated aromatics in small measure
Let it boil until dry, then moisten with broth and finish cooking it over gentle heat to make it tender, which will take 7 to 8 hours total; if the broth runs out, help yourself with more broth
When ready to serve, enhance the flavor with parmesan and pour it over slices of toasted bread that should be swimming in the broth
Sufficient for five people

title: Uova di Neve (Floating Islands)
description: Prepared with powdered sugar, milk, and sugar.
steps: Put the milk on the fire in a wide pan and while it heats, beat with a whisk the egg whites that you will have already separated from the yolks; but throw into them a pinch of salt if it is true that it serves to strengthen the consistency.

When the whites are well beaten, take the perforated shaker where powdered sugar is ordinarily kept and, continuing always to beat them, throw in enough to make them somewhat sweet. Twenty or thirty grams of powdered sugar may suffice, but it is better to taste them.
This done, take up the beaten whites with a tablespoon, and giving them the approximate shape of an egg, throw them into the milk when it boils.
Turn these so-called eggs to cook them on all sides and when you see them set, take them with a slotted spoon and put them to drain in a colander.
Strain that milk and, when it is cold, make with the same, with the yolks and with sugar a cream like that of No. 685, giving it the flavor of vanilla.
Arrange on a platter the floating islands in fine display, one on top of the other, pour the cream over them and serve them cold.

title: Uova Ripiene I (Stuffed Eggs I)
description: Prepared with eggs, anchovies, and onion.
steps: After hard-boiling the eggs, cut them in half lengthwise and extract the yolks.
Take one anchovy for every two eggs, wash them, remove the bone, and chop them finely with a little parsley and very little onion.
Mix in the yolks and enough butter so that you can knead everything together with a knife blade.
Fill the cavities left by the yolks with this mixture and arrange the stuffed egg halves neatly on a platter.
Cover them with mayonnaise sauce (recipe N. 126).
They can also be eaten simply seasoned with salt, pepper, oil and vinegar, and they are quite palatable; it also seems that the stomach is not offended by them.

title: Vitello Tonnato (Veal with Tuna Sauce)
description: A sauce made with milk or veal, anchovies, and onion.

ingredients.name: milk-fed veal from the thigh or rump, all in one piece and boneless
ingredients.sourceText: 1 kilogram of milk-fed veal from the thigh or rump, all in one piece and boneless

ingredients.name: canned tuna in oil
ingredients.sourceText: 100 grams of canned tuna in oil

steps: Take {{source-0}}, remove the thin skin and fat, then lard it with two anchovies.
Wash the anchovies, split them in two, remove the spine, and cut them crosswise making eight pieces total.

Tie the meat not too tightly and put it to boil for an hour and a half in enough water to cover it, in which you have put a quarter of an onion studded with two cloves, a bay leaf, celery, carrot, and parsley.
Salt the water generously and wait for it to boil before putting in the meat.
When cooked, untie it, dry it, and when cold cut it into thin slices and keep it soaking for a day or two in a narrow vessel in the following sauce in sufficient quantity to cover it.

Pound {{source-8}} and two anchovies, break them down well with a knife blade or better pass them through a sieve, adding fine oil in abundance little by little and the juice of a lemon or even more so that the sauce comes out liquid.
Finally mix in a handful of capers squeezed of vinegar.
Serve the veal with tuna sauce with its sauce and with lemon wedges.
Strain the broth and use it for a risotto.

title: Zucchini Fritti II (Fried Zucchini II)
description: Prepared with zucchini, salt, and flour.
steps: Take large and thick zucchini that cannot be grasped with one hand. Peel them to make the fried dish more beautiful, open them in two parts lengthwise and remove the pulp from the part that shows the seeds. Then cut them into long and thin strips, a finger's width wide and place them with salt to make water, leaving them there for several hours. When you are about to fry them take them up with both hands and squeeze them hard to press out the water that they still contain, then throw them into flour loosening them with your fingers, then into the small sieve and throw them immediately in a pan with plenty of fat.

title: Zuppa alla Certosina (Carthusian Soup)
description: A soup made with fish, onion, and celery.

ingredients.name: small fish of various species
ingredients.sourceText: 500 grams of small fish of various species

ingredients.name: Butter, oil, or lard for frying
ingredients.sourceText: Butter, oil, or lard for frying

steps: Make a battuto with a quarter of an onion, parsley, and celery.
Put it on the fire with oil.
When it has colored, add the fish, moistening it when dry with water, tomato juice, or conserve.
Season with salt and pepper.
Let it cook well, then add the necessary water for the soup: about one liter or slightly more in total can suffice.
Pass everything through a sieve or strainer, pressing well, and return it to the fire to bring it to a boil.
In the soup tureen, beat together two eggs with three tablespoons of Parmesan cheese beforehand.
Pour the broth slowly and gradually into the tureen with the egg mixture.
Before sending the soup to the table, add the bread, which, in small dice, can be simply toasted or fried in butter, oil, or lard as you prefer.
The eggs and Parmesan can also be beaten separately and poured into the pot when the broth is boiling, stirring strongly, if you do not mind seeing them set in shreds.

title: Zuppa alla Spagnuola (Spanish Soup)
description: A soup made with chicken breast, broth, and bread.

ingredients.name: Chicken breast (petto di pollastra o di cappone)
ingredients.sourceText: Chicken breast (petto di pollastra o di cappone)

steps: Cut the chicken breast into small pieces and cook slowly in butter, seasoning with salt and pepper
If needed, moisten with broth
Remove the cooked chicken and keep aside
In the remaining sauce, add a bread crumb about the size of a fist and make a thick paste with broth
Place this paste and the cooked chicken in a mortar
Add two egg yolks and a pinch of nutmeg, pound everything finely
Leave the mixture in a cool place to set
When ready to use (can be the next day), dust a work surface with flour
Form the mixture into a stick about the thickness of a finger or less
Cut with a floured knife into equal pieces
Round them into small balls the size of a hazelnut or smaller, using flour-dusted hands
Drop into boiling broth and cook for five or six minutes
Serve in a bowl lined with bread cubes fried in butter or virgin lard
Serves ten to twelve people

Place this paste and the cooked chicken in a mortar
Add two egg yolks and a pinch of nutmeg, pound everything finely
Leave the mixture in a cool place to set
When ready to use (can be the next day), dust a work surface with flour
Form the mixture into a stick about the thickness of a finger or less
Cut with a floured knife into equal pieces
Round them into small balls the size of a hazelnut or smaller, using flour-dusted hands
Drop into boiling broth and cook for five or six minutes
Serve in a bowl lined with bread cubes fried in butter or virgin lard
Serves ten to twelve people

title: Zuppa col Brodo di Muggine (Soup with Mullet Broth)
description: A soup made with mullet, onion, and garlic.

ingredients.name: One mullet (or baldigara), weighing at least one kilogram
ingredients.sourceText: One mullet (or baldigara), weighing at least one kilogram

steps: Scrape the scales from the mullet, clean it, and boil it with water in proportion.
Make a generous battuto with onion, garlic, parsley, carrot, and celery.
Put this mixture on the fire with oil, salt, and pepper.
When it has taken color, stop it with tomato juice and let it boil with the fish broth.
Strain this broth and with a little of the same broth cook a small quantity of celery, carrot, and dried mushrooms, all cut into small pieces, which serve to give flavor.
Toast the bread for the soup and cut it into dice.
Put the bread in the soup tureen and pour the hot broth over it along with the said flavoring vegetables.
Serve at the table with Parmesan cheese on the side.

title: Zuppa di Fagiuoli (Bean Soup)
description: A soup made with beans, onion, and garlic.

ingredients.name: A nice piece of white celery
ingredients.sourceText: A nice piece of white celery

steps: Choose beans with fine skin or pass them; those with eyes have less of this defect than others.

Make a soffritto in this proportion: take a quarter onion, one garlic clove, a pinch of parsley and a nice piece of white celery. Chop these aromatics very finely with a crescent knife and put them on the fire with a good measure of oil; be generous with pepper.
When the soffritto has taken color, add two ladle-fuls of the bean broth, add a little tomato juice or paste, let them come to a boil and pour it into the pot of beans.
For those who like a little greens in the soup, you can add cavolo nero, first boiled and then cooked a bit in the liquid of the aforesaid soffritto.
Now all that remains is to dampen the bread, already prepared beforehand with thick slices toasted and then cut into cubes.

title: Zuppa di ovoli (Caesar's Mushroom Soup)
description: A soup made with mushrooms, lard, and parmesan cheese.

ingredients.name: Caesar's mushrooms (ovoli), 600 grams before cleaning (about 500 grams after)
ingredients.sourceText: Caesar's mushrooms (ovoli), 600 grams before cleaning (about 500 grams after)

ingredients.name: One whole egg and one yolk
ingredients.sourceText: One whole egg and one yolk

steps: Clean and peel the mushrooms, then wash them whole and cut them into small, thin slices or pieces.
Make a soffritto (sauté mixture) with 50 grams of lard and a pinch of parsley and put it on the fire with 50 grams of butter and three spoonfuls of oil.
When it has softened, pour in the mushrooms and salt them somewhat to give them partial cooking, then pour them into the broth with all the soffritto to let them boil another ten minutes.

Before removing from heat, break a whole egg and one yolk in the tureen with a handful of grated Parmesan and pour the soup over it little by little stirring, then add dice of toasted bread; but note that the soup should remain very brothy.
This dose will serve six or seven persons.
If you make half the amount, only the whole egg will suffice.

title: Zuppa di Ranocchi (Frog Soup)
description: A soup made with carrot, celery, and onion.
steps: Remove the thighs from the frogs and set them aside.
Make a generous battuto (finely chopped mixture) with two cloves of garlic, parsley, carrot, celery, and basil if desired; or use onion if you dislike garlic.
Put this mixture on the fire with salt, pepper, and a good measure of oil.
When the garlic begins to take color, add the frogs.
Stir them from time to time so they do not stick.
When they have released a good portion of their liquid, add pieces of tomatoes or, if lacking, diluted tomato conserve with water.
Continue to boil, and finally add the necessary water to make soup, keeping everything on the fire until the frogs are cooked and falling apart.
Pass everything through a sieve, pressing well so that only the small bones remain.
Put the thighs set aside earlier to boil in a little of this strained broth.
Debone them when cooked and mix them into the soup along with pieces of dried mushrooms that have been softened.
Toast bread into slices, then cut into rather large dice.
Serve the soup with the toasted bread dice.

ingredients.name: Virgin lard or oil or butter for frying

steps: Mince together the half breast of capon or chicken, the slice of ham, and the piece of marrow.
Season it with grated Parmesan, give it the scent of nutmeg and bind it with an egg. Salt is not necessary as there is ham.
Take a small loaf of stale bread, slice it round to the thickness of half a finger, remove the crust from the slices and on half of them spread the aforesaid mixture.
On each of these spread slices, lay a slice without mixture and press them together so they stick.
Then cut these paired slices into small dice and fry them in virgin lard or oil or butter, according to the taste of the region or your own.
When it is time to serve the soup at table, place the fried dice in the tureen and pour boiling broth over them.

steps: Prepare a good meat gravy (see N. 5)
Cut the potato and zucchini into chunks, all the others into strips
Boil all the vegetables and then sauté them in butter, wetting them with the said gravy
Keep the bread slices half a finger thick, toast them and cut them into cubes

Take a pan or, better, a similar vessel, decent enough because it must be brought to table, and in this prepare the soup in the following manner: a layer of bread, one of vegetables and over it a sprinkling of Parmesan, and so on
Finally pour the gravy over it and, without touching it, cover it with a plate and a towel and keep it for half an hour in warmth near the fire before serving it
Note that this soup should remain almost dry, so it is well to hold back a little gravy to add when you send it to table, in case it turns out too dry

While they boil, make a mixture with a quarter of a large onion and two cloves of garlic, two pieces of celery a palm long and a good pinch of parsley.

Chop it finely, put it on the fire with the oil mentioned above and when it has taken color, pour into it the vegetables cut roughly, first the cabbages, then the beet greens and the potato cut into pieces.
Season with salt and pepper and then add tomato juice or conserve, and if during boiling they become somewhat dry, moisten them with the bean broth.

When the beans are cooked, throw a quarter of them, left whole, among the vegetables, adding the rinds; pass the others through a sieve and dissolve them in the broth, pouring also this into the vessel where the vegetables are.
Mix, let boil a little more and pour everything into the tureen where you have already placed the bread cut into thin slices and cover it to serve after about twenty minutes.
This quantity may be enough for six people; it is good hot and better cold.

Some strips of dried pork or prosciutto rind
sourceSteps: Put the beans on the fire with the water mentioned, adding the rind.
While they boil, make a mixture with a quarter of a large onion and two cloves of garlic, two pieces of celery a palm long and a good pinch of parsley.

Chop it finely, put it on the fire with the oil mentioned above and when it has taken color, pour into it the vegetables cut roughly, first the cabbages, then the beet greens and the potato cut into pieces.
Season with salt and pepper and then add tomato juice or conserve, and if during boiling they become somewhat dry, moisten them with the bean broth.

When the beans are cooked, throw a quarter of them, left whole, among the vegetables, adding the rinds; pass the others through a sieve and dissolve them in the broth, pouring also this into the vessel where the vegetables are.
Mix, let boil a little more and pour everything into the tureen where you have already placed the bread cut into thin slices and cover it to serve after about twenty minutes.
This quantity may be enough for six people; it is good hot and better cold.

ingredients.name: sugar per twelve pounds of fruit

Place them in a pot with cold water
Place on the fire
When the water trembles and the apricots rise to the top, carefully remove them with a skimmer

For twelve pounds of fruit, clarify three pounds of sugar
When it reaches the pearl stage, add the apricots
Let them reach five or six boils
Remove them from the syrup and remove from the heat
Let the apricots drain

title: Ailerons au Soleil (Turkey Wings au Soleil)
description: Prepared with turkey, velouté, and bouillon.
steps: Sauté your twelve wings in butter as for chipolata
Add eight spoonfuls of Velouté, half a pot spoonful of bouillon, a bay leaf, coarse pepper, a clove, a bouquet of parsley and chives
Bring your wings to a boil; skim them
Three-quarters cooked, degrease them
When they are cooked, reduce your sauce so that it is well thickened
Remove the bouquet, leaf and clove
Add a liaison of three egg yolks into your ragout, with butter the size of half an egg
When it is thickened, place your wings to cool on a cake pan or platter, and their sauce on top
After this, coat them well with their sauce, and put them in bread crumbs
Then place them in an omelet of five raw eggs
Bread them a second time equally so that the sauce does not run into the frying oil
Give your wings a beautiful form
At the moment of serving

title: Ailerons de Dindons aux Petits Oignons et au Fromage (Turkey Wings with Small Onions and Cheese)
description: Prepared with turkey, onions, and bay leaf.

ingredients.name: at least a dozen small onions
ingredients.sourceText: at least a dozen small onions

steps: Blanch the turkey wings, clean them, and place them in a saucepan with a bouquet of parsley, chives, two cloves, half a bay leaf, and a little basil
Moisten with one glass of white wine and an equal amount of broth
Cook over low heat
After half an hour, add at least a dozen small onions blanched for a quarter-hour in boiling water and well cleaned
Season lightly with salt and coarse pepper
Finish cooking and remove the wings and onions from the pan to drain them
Strain the sauce through a sieve and reduce it if too thin
Add a piece of butter worked with a pinch of flour and thicken over the fire
Put a little sauce in the bottom of the serving plat and cover with a handful of grated Gruyère or Parmesan
Arrange the wings and small onions on top, pour the remaining sauce over everything, and cover with more grated cheese
Place the plat on a small stove to simmer over low heat until almost no sauce remains
Brown the top with a hot shovel or a tourière cover with good heat and serve hot

title: Artichauts (Artichokes)
description: Prepared with artichokes, water, and salt.

ingredients.name: three artichokes of the same size
ingredients.sourceText: three artichokes of the same size

steps: Take three artichokes of the same size and remove what is hard found at the heart
Trim the leaves by removing the tips
Wash them well and place them in a pot with boiling salted water
Ensure they are submerged in water
After one hour, ensure they are cooked
Remove them from the boiling water and place them in cold water
Remove the choke
At the moment of serving, place them in boiling water
Drain them and place them on a plate with white or brown sauce inside or in a sauceboat

title: Artichauts au Velouté (Artichokes with Velouté Sauce)
description: A sauce made with artichokes, velouté, and consommé.

ingredients.name: butter, the size of an egg
ingredients.sourceText: butter, the size of an egg

steps: Trim the heart of the artichokes; if they are large, cut them into eight pieces
Trim the leaves and remove the choke
Place the pieces in water, drain them, and arrange them in a pot
Add pepper, five spoonfuls of velouté sauce, six spoonfuls of consommé, and butter the size of an egg
Half an hour before serving, place them on the fire to boil vigorously
Place fire on the pot cover
Arrange the artichokes on the plate when cooked
If you have no sauce, make a light roux, moisten it with broth, and pour it over the artichokes

title: Artichauts Frits (Fried Artichokes)
description: Prepared with artichokes, egg yolks, and vinegar.
steps: Peel the heart of two artichokes and cut each into twelve pieces
Place them in water to wash; let them drain
Place them in a terrine or pot with salt, pepper, 2 tablespoons of oil, one whole egg, two egg yolks, three tablespoons of vinegar, eight tablespoons of flour, and half a glass of beer

Stir them so they are coated with batter all over

title: Artichauts à la Barigoule (Artichokes Barigoule)
description: Prepared with artichokes, lard, and mushrooms.

ingredients.name: butter and oil in equal amounts
ingredients.sourceText: butter and oil in equal amounts

steps: Cut off the tips of the leaves; place three artichokes in water
When well washed, place them in a pot of boiling water and blanch for twenty minutes
Refresh them and remove the choke; let them drain
Take hot fat and place the artichokes in it with the leaf side down; when the leaves are well fried, drain them
Add a quarter pound of minced lard to a pot, along with equal amounts of butter and oil
Chop mushrooms very fine and pass them through the pot
Add a tablespoon of finely chopped shallots, the same of parsley, a little spice, salt, and coarse pepper
Pass the herbs well and let them cool, then place them inside the artichokes
Line the bottom of a pot with lard strips and a few veal slices
Truss your artichokes and place them in the pot with thyme, bay leaf, and a glass of bouillon
Cover with lard strips and a round of buttered paper
When boiling, place on low heat and put hot coals on the lid
After braising for three-quarters of an hour, remove the twine and serve on a platter
Pour a little espagnole sauce inside; if you have no sauce, make a light roux that you moisten with the braising liquid from the artichokes and pass through a silk sieve

title: Artichauts à la Lyonnaise (Artichokes Lyonnaise Style)
description: Prepared with artichokes, butter, and salt.
steps: If the three artichokes are large, cut them into eight pieces
Remove the hard part found at the heart, the choke, and the leaves until only three or four remain
Reduce their width
Place them in water as you trim them
Wash them well and drain them
Put half a pound of butter in the bottom of your pot, spread it well, and place the artichoke heart on top
Sprinkle salt and pepper on the artichokes
Half an hour before serving, place them on a moderately hot fire and place fire on the pot cover as well
Take care that they do not burn
When cooked, arrange them on the plate and pour the butter over them
You may also sauté them in butter on a hot fire; when they are browned, they are ready

title: Artichauts à la Provençale (Artichokes Provençal)
description: Prepared with artichokes, onions, and anchovies.
steps: Prepare three artichokes as for artichokes barigoule
Cut twelve onions into four pieces, about one line thick, each piece forming a quarter circle
Put half a pound of oil in a pot and place it on the fire with the onions inside
When the onions are well browned, pound three anchovies and mix them with butter and the onions
Put the mixture inside the artichokes
Cook them in a pot as described for artichokes barigoule
When serving, pour espagnole sauce inside, or make a light roux that you moisten with the braising liquid from the artichokes
You may also cook them simply on a lard strip with heat above and below

title: Artichaux Confit pour l'Hiver (Pickled Artichokes for Winter)
description: Prepared with artichokes and water.
steps: Remove all the leaves and leave only what is good to eat on the heart
Throw them in water until you have prepared them all
Cook them afterward in water until you can easily remove the choke
Put them back in fresh water
When they are well cleaned, put them to drain
If it is to dry them, put them on hurdles in an oven that should not be too hot; if you can hold your hand in it without it burning you, that is enough
When they are dry, you will serve them to put in stews after having made them revive in lukewarm water
If you wish to pickle them, they will be better; put a brine as is explained for pickled green beans and follow the same method

title: Artichokes Preserved for Winter
description: Prepared with artichokes, water, and salt.
steps: After washing artichokes well, let them drain
Trim the base by removing the stem and cutting off the outer surface
Have a large pot three-quarters full of water with two handfuls of salt
When the water boils, add about a dozen artichokes
Let them boil; after a quarter hour, remove them and place in cold water
Let them drain for five or six hours
Arrange them in a large earthenware pot or butter pot
Pour brine over them so they are covered; also add one or two pounds of oil depending on the width of your dish
To cook, place in cold water on the fire and boil until cooked, then cool and remove the fuzzy center
Serve with sauce or in another manner

title: Asperges (Asparagus)
description: Prepared with asparagus, salt, and oil.
steps: The asparagus of Rony is preferred for taste and thickness.
Remove the leaves down to the bouquet with the knife blade near the tip.
Scrape away the outer layer from the bouquet to the end of the white part.
Make sure they are all the same length.
Tie them in bundles.
Twenty minutes before serving, put them in boiling salted water.
Test them by bending; if they are tender, refresh them so they do not cook too much and do not lose their green color.
If you want them with oil, serve them cold in a single bundle; they must be regularly arranged on the plate.

title: Aspic de Blanc de Poulet (Aspic of Chicken Breast)
description: Prepared with chicken, aspic, and velouté.
steps: Sauté eight chicken breasts.
Season them with salt and coarse pepper.
Let them cool on a platter.
Pour into a casserole four degrease-spoonfuls of velouté and four spoonfuls of jelly.
Reduce everything to half its volume.
Add a liaison of one egg yolk, a little chopped and washed parsley, and an amount of butter the size of half an egg, added after your sauce is bound.
Blend it well with your sauce.
Pour it over your fillets.
Let it cool thoroughly until well congealed.
Arrange aspic in your mold to a thickness of about half an inch.
Put it in cold storage.
When well congealed, decorate it.
Arrange your fillets symmetrically with correct form and smooth top due to the sauce that masked them.
On top of your fillets arrange a small cold ragout of crests and kidneys with the fillets mignons placed in a similar sauce.
Then pour melted aspic to fill your mold and add it when cold.
Let your aspic congeal well.
At serving time, invert it and detach it as directed for aspic.

title: Aubergines (Eggplants)
description: Prepared with eggplants, lard, and mushrooms.
steps: Cut four eggplants in half lengthwise without hollowing out too much so they retain some flesh
Grate lard twice the size of an egg and the same amount of butter
Heat four large spoonfuls of oil in a saucepan
Add two large spoonfuls of finely chopped mushrooms, a small handful of shallots and one of parsley
Cook these fine herbs with the butter, lard and oil
When well browned, add salt, coarse pepper, a little spice and let cool
Add as much cooked quenelle forcemeat as you have fine herbs
Chop three anchovies and mix with the forcemeat and herbs
Fill the eight eggplant halves with this mixture
Smooth the top of the forcemeat with egg and bread
Half an hour before serving, place on a baking sheet in the oven or over moderate heat with a camp oven on top

title: Autre Canard aux Navets (Another Duck with Turnips)
description: Prepared with duck, turnips, and bouillon.

ingredients.name: one duck, cleaned, singed and trussed

ingredients.name: a bouquet of parsley and chives

steps: When your duck is cleaned, singed and trussed, make a roux
When it is well blonde, put your duck in it and let it brown
When the meat is firm everywhere, pour in two spoonfuls of bouillon; if you lack bouillon, add water, salt, pepper, and a bay leaf
Turn your duck with its liquid until it boils
Add a bouquet of parsley and chives and let it cook on high heat
When your duck is three-quarters cooked, add turnips that you have shaped to uniform size
Sauté them in butter; when they are well blonde, let them drain
Put them with your duck and cook on low heat
Degrease the duck and add a small piece of sugar
At service time, unbind it and pour your ragout of turnips over it. Check that it is properly seasoned

title: Aux Grenouilles (Frog Soup)
description: A soup made with bread, milk or broth, and butter.

ingredients.name: bread crumb, tender, weighing a quarter pound
ingredients.sourceText: bread crumb, tender, weighing a quarter pound

steps: You cut the head of the frog; you pull the body from its skin, observing to remove the entrails; the thighs and the neck, which you will make disgorge, must be very clean; you need about fifty; you put them in a saucepan with a good piece of butter, salt, coarse pepper, a little nutmeg; you sauté your frogs on the fire; when they have been on a good fire for ten minutes, you then put them on a gentler heat for half an hour so that they finish cooking; you must drain them and put them cooked in a mortar; you add a piece of tender bread weighing a quarter pound; you soak it in milk or broth; you pound it all together; when you have pounded it for a quarter hour, and your frogs are well in paste, you put them in a saucepan, and you thin them with the juice they have rendered; you pass it all through a fine sieve; if this were not liquid enough, you will take broth that you intend for your soup; pass your purée to make it liquid, and put it on gentle heat; try that it does not boil: you will have bread crusts that you prepare as for bread soup; you will boil a little broth, which you will pour over your crusts a quarter hour before serving; and at the moment of serving your soup you will pour your frog purée over your bread; try that your soup is neither too thick nor too clear. This soup is made with fat as well as lean. (See Lean Broth.)

title: Beef Tongue Hochepot Style (Langue de Bœuf en hochepot)
description: Prepared with beef tongue, carrots, and espagnole.
steps: Prepare the tongue and cook it as for the gherkin version
Cut it into slices and arrange in miroton style
Around the plate have carrots turned into small batons, which you will blanch
Refresh and drain them and put them in a pan
Add three spoonfuls of espagnole and five of consommé and a small piece of sugar
Cook them; at the time of serving, arrange the tongue and glaze it, and put the small roots in the middle around the plate
Make a border of small glazed onions; or if you have neither sauce nor consommé, after blanching the small roots, sauté them in a pan with a small piece of butter
Dust them with half a spoonful of flour
Pass the cooking liquid from the tongue through a silk sieve and moisten the small roots with it
The sauce should be thin so that you may reduce it
When cooking the small roots, take care to degrease them well and add a little coarse pepper

Cook them in hot fat until it is a beautiful color
Serve them

title: Beignets Soufflés, ou Pets et Petits Choux (Puffed Fritters, or Small Choux)
description: Prepared with lemons, orange flower water, and butter.

ingredients.name: butter the size of an egg
ingredients.sourceText: butter the size of an egg

ingredients.name: orange flower water, one full teaspoonful
ingredients.sourceText: orange flower water, one full teaspoonful

steps: Put in a saucepan butter the size of an egg, two grated green lemons, one full teaspoonful of orange flower water, a quarteron of sugar, a little salt, and a large half-setier of water
Boil everything together for a moment
Add enough flour to make a well-bound and very thick paste
Stir it well on the fire with a wooden spoon until it sticks to the saucepan
Transfer it promptly to another saucepan and mix in two eggs at a time, stirring well with your wooden spoon
Continue adding two eggs at a time until your paste becomes soft without being runny
Spread it on a plate to the thickness of a finger with a knife
Heat some fat, not too hot
Dip the handle of a ragout spoon in the fat and take paste with it the size of a walnut
Drop it in the pan by striking the edge
Fry at a gentle fire, stirring constantly
When they are well-puffed and a beautiful color, serve them hot after dusting with fine sugar
Alternatively, make small mounds of paste the size of a walnut close together on white paper
Turn them into fat more than half-hot
When your fritters detach, remove the paper and fry them the same way
With this same paste, you can make small choux, with only the changes of putting more butter in the paste and cooking them in the oven

Fry at a gentle fire, stirring constantly

title: Bisque (Crayfish Bisque)
description: Prepared with crayfish, rice, and broth or water.
steps: You will take fifty crayfish that you will wash in eight or ten waters; you will put them in a saucepan, adding salt, coarse pepper, a little grated nutmeg and a quarter pound of butter; you will put them on a fairly hot fire; you will sauté or stir them with a spoon for a quarter hour. When your crayfish are cooked, you will let them drain, and you will remove the meat that you will pound. You must make rice burst for a quarter hour in broth or water; you will drain it and put it in the mortar with your crayfish meat; when it is all well pounded, you will put it in a saucepan, and thin it with a little soup broth that you will pass through a fine sieve; when your purée is made, you will thin it with broth so that it is neither too thick nor too clear, then you will pound the crayfish shells; when they are well pounded, you will put juice in them, or the butter in which your crayfish were cooked, and you will pass this purée through a fine sieve. It should then have a red color. You will put it in a saucepan on gentle heat; try that neither one nor the other purées boil, but that they are very hot; you will have crusts from the top of the bread, that you will put in your soup tureen, and you will pour a little extremely hot broth over your bread before serving; then, at the moment of service, you will pour your first purée over your bread, and as for the one of shells, you will pour it over your soup with a large spoon, so that it has a beautiful color. This soup is made with fat as well as lean. (See Lean Broth.)

title: Blanquette de Veau aux champignons (Veal Blanquette with Mushrooms)
description: Prepared with veal, mushrooms, and velouté or flour or bouillon.

ingredients.name: Veal loin, underside, roasted on the spit
ingredients.sourceText: Veal loin, underside, roasted on the spit

steps: Place the underside of veal loin on the spit; when cooked, let it cool.
Slice it, beat the pieces with the flat of your knife blade.
Cut off the angles and round your pieces as much as possible; try to make them equal.
Put them in a casserole as they are cut and trimmed; use only the white meat and remove everything that has the color of the spit.
Have mushrooms that you will turn (shape); cut them thick about one line, forming a round shape.
Sauté them in butter.
When they are sautéed, put them with the meat of your blanquette.
Pour into the butter where they cooked four spoonfuls to degrease of velouté, or more if your blanquette is strong, and just over three spoonfuls of consommé.
Degrease your sauce, reduce it, and pass it through a sieve over your blanquette.
Keep it warm without it boiling.
At the moment of serving, add to it a liaison of two egg yolks, or more if your blanquette is strong, a little coarse pepper.
Stir gently your blanquette on the edge of the stove.
When your liaison is in and when you see that your sauce is thickened, remove it, always stirring.
Check if it is of good salt and good taste; then arrange it in a pyramid.
Try to ensure there is not too much sauce.

Add mushrooms if you have them.
Pass through your butter chopped parsley and chives.

When it is thickened, add to it a little verjuice or a dash of vinegar.

description: Prepared with carrots and broth.

ingredients.name: Two calf necks and two calf knuckles
ingredients.sourceText: Two calf necks and two calf knuckles

steps: Put in a round saucepan two calf necks and two calf knuckles, four carrots and four onions
Moisten them with two spoonfuls of great broth
Place your saucepan on a good stove

When the glaze at the bottom of your saucepan is of beautiful color, fill it with great broth
Be careful to skim it so that your blond is not cloudy
Do not add salt, since your great broth is seasoned

title: Boudin (Blood Sausage)
description: Prepared with blood, onions, and lard or butter.

ingredients.name: Three to four pounds of pork fat, diced
ingredients.sourceText: Three to four pounds of pork fat, diced

steps: Cut thirty or forty onions into dice; remove the head and tail, and let them melt gently in white by passing them over the fire with lard or butter
When well melted, add three or four pounds of pork fat also cut into dice; combine with your onions
Add parsley and chives, spices, salt, and black pepper, stirring into four pints of blood
Add one pint of cream; mix everything together so that your fat does not remain in lumps
Have intestines that you will have washed, and funnel your mixture into your intestines; avoid trapping air inside
When your intestine is full, tie it at the end to the size you desire
Have a pot full of water whose heat is too hot to hold your finger in; place your boudin in it
Do not let the water boil, to avoid bursting it: test it; remove it when it begins to be firm, and when pricked it no longer runs blood
Then slice your boudin and grill it

description: Prepared with onions, pork fat, and bread crumbs.

ingredients.name: Meat from a roasted fowl, cooked
ingredients.sourceText: Meat from a roasted fowl, cooked

steps: Cut onions into very small dice; cook them as the previous ones; add pounded pork fat that you mix with your onions

Add bread crumbs that you have made by drying them in milk; take the meat from a roasted fowl that you chop, and that you pound with your bread crumbs, using equal amounts of bread crumbs, fowl, and fat
Add one chopine of good cream; thin your fowl mixture; add six egg yolks, salt, and your spices; mix everything together
Pour it into your intestines: cook them in milk cut with water; do not let it boil, to avoid your boudin bursting
When it is cold, prick it; grill it on an oiled sheet of paper that you place on the grill over a gentle fire: serve this boudin as an appetizer
With this method of making boudin, you may use hare, young rabbits, pheasants, partridge, veal, or pork

title: Boudin Blanc à la Bourgeoise (White Sausage in the Bourgeois Style)
description: Prepared with bread, onions, and pork belly.

ingredients.name: Crumb of bread, a good handful
ingredients.sourceText: Crumb of bread, a good handful

ingredients.name: Pork belly fat (panne), half a pound, chopped
ingredients.sourceText: Pork belly fat (panne), half a pound, chopped

ingredients.name: Cream, a little more than half a setier
ingredients.sourceText: Cream, a little more than half a setier

steps: Put on the fire a chopine of good milk that you bring to a boil and add a good handful of bread crumbs, pass through a sieve
Boil everything together turning often, principally toward the end, until the bread crumb has absorbed all the milk and is well thick
Set it to cool
Cut half a dozen onions into small dice and cook them on a small fire without coloring them, with a piece of butter
After they are removed from the fire, add the bread crumb with six egg yolks and a little more than half a setier of cream
Mix everything together, season with fine salt and fine spices
Take pork intestines well washed, cut them to the length you wish to make the sausages, fill them only three-quarters full, tie the end
When they are all finished, boil water; when it boils vigorously, gently put in the sausages and boil them until they are cooked, which takes only a quarter hour
You will know they are cooked by pricking them with a pin, fat will come out
Remove them gently with a skimmer, put them in fresh water, let them drain, and grill them in a paper case, then remove them from the case to serve them hot

ingredients.name: pork intestines, about eight inches long
ingredients.sourceText: pork intestines, about eight inches long

steps: Boil the milk with three sliced onions, coriander, parsley, whole chives, thyme, bay leaf, and basil
Reduce this milk to one third
When reduced and passed through a sieve, add several chopped rabbit livers, panne cut into small squares, a little fine salt, and fine spices
Mix in ten egg yolks and heat everything over a small fire, stirring constantly
When well mixed and not too hot, stuff this mixture into pork intestines about eight inches long, filling them only two-thirds as they will swell during cooking
Cook them in boiling water for a quarter hour
Test if cooked by pricking with a pin; if fat comes out, they are cooked
Remove them into fresh water and then place on a plate to grill
Serve dry as an appetizer

steps: When you do not have grand bouillon of consommé but you have a little meat, mark a great sauce as you can
Have one or two pounds of beef slice (according to the size of the sauce) and two or three pounds of veal
Add poultry trimmings, whatever you have
Put some carrots and some onions
Put everything in a casserole
Put a full pot-spoonful of water in it
Put your meats on a somewhat hot fire
When there is almost no more moistening in your casserole, put it on a gentle fire so the glaze at the bottom of your casserole colors without burning
When it is a dark blonde and your glaze is brown, moisten it with water if you do not have bouillon
Then put in a strong bouquet of parsley and chives and two bay leaves

title: Béchamel (Béchamel Sauce)
description: A sauce made with velouté, consommé, and cream.
steps: Place the velouté in a saucepan
Add the consommé
Reduce over high heat, stirring constantly, from eleven spoonfuls to five
In a separate pot, place the cream on high heat and reduce by half
Stir the cream constantly with a wooden spoon and scrape the bottom so it does not stick and does not take on a burnt taste
Mix the reduced velouté and cream together
Bring to a boil over high heat, stirring constantly so the sauce thickens and does not stick
Stir the béchamel for three-quarters of an hour to one hour
When the sauce is sufficiently thickened, strain through a sieve
The sauce should be a yellowish white

title: Bœuf au Four (Beef Baked in the Oven)
description: Prepared with beef, beef fat, and bacon.

ingredients.name: Lean bacon, cut into small dice
ingredients.sourceText: Lean bacon, cut into small dice

steps: Take as much beef chuck as you judge appropriate and mince it with half as much beef fat

Put the meat in a casserole with lean bacon cut into small dice, parsley, chives, mushrooms, two shallots, all minced very fine, salt, coarse pepper, a glass of brandy, and four egg yolks; mix everything together well
Line a casserole or terrine of the size of your meat with lard strips
Put the meat on top, pressed down well
Cover with a lid and seal the edges with flour mixed with a little vinegar
Bake in the oven for three or four hours
If serving hot as an entrée, remove the lard strips and degrease the sauce; for a side dish, let it cool in its cooking liquid

title: Cabillaud, ou Morue fraîche (Fresh Cod)
description: Prepared with cod and water.
steps: Clean out your cod and wash it
Make well salted water, because the fish only takes up what is needed
When the water is clear, tie the head of your fish
Put it in the fish cooker with the salted water over it
Cook it over a very small fire
If serving it as a main course, add a cream sauce; if it is for a roast, serve it plain on a platter with a napkin and parsley leaves around it
You can also cook it in a court-bouillon like the turbot

title: Cailles au Chasseur (Sautéed Quail, Hunter's Style)
description: Prepared with quail, bay leaf, and white wine.
steps: Clean and singe your quail.
Put a piece of butter in a saucepan with your quail inside, a bay leaf, salt, pepper, and a little fine herbs if you have them.
Place your quail over a hot fire and sauté them constantly.
When they resist under your finger, take a spoonful of flour which you mix with your quail, a half-glass of white wine, and a little bouillon.
When your sauce is thickened, remove your quail from the fire; they must not boil.
Arrange them on the plate and check that they are well seasoned.

title: Cailles au Fumé de Gibier (Quails with Game Essence)
description: Prepared with quails, game, and quail.
steps: Remove the breast bones from your quail from the inside without damaging the outside
After cleaning it through the cavity, singe it lightly
Take fillets from other quails and season them with a little salt, coarse pepper, a little finely chopped parsley, a quarter pound of butter, and the juice of a lemon
Put two in each quail; you need eight quails for an entrée
Truss them and round them as well as possible
Baste them so they keep their shape while cooking
Put a good piece of butter in a saucepan with the juice of a lemon and a bay leaf
Stiffen your quails for a moment in your butter
Put strips of bacon in a saucepan, your quails on top of them
Cover them also with strips of bacon and put a pan moistened with white wine over your quails
Cook them over heat for a good half hour
Before serving and at the moment of doing so, drain them, remove the trussing strings, and arrange them on your plate
Put an espagnole sauce prepared with game essence on top; if you have no sauce, make a light roux and pass through a silk sieve the cooking liquid in which your quails cooked
Pour it over your roux and add a spoonful of jus
Reduce your sauce by half, skim off the fat and pass it through a sieve, then place it under your quails
If your sauce had too much salt, add the juice of half a lemon and a piece of fresh butter the size of a walnut, melting it by stirring into your sauce without putting it on the fire
If the fillets are too difficult to obtain for putting inside your quails, you may chop the livers which you will mix with a little farce

title: Cailles au Gratin (Quail au Gratin)
description: Prepared with quail, forcemeat, and velouté.
steps: Bone ten fresh quail and set the livers aside.
Pound all the livers with the back of a knife.
Have a cooked forcemeat in which you put your pounded livers with a little coarse pepper, very little salt, and a little pounded aromatics.
Mix everything together and fill your quail with this forcemeat.
Give them their original shape and secure them with a needle and thread.
Pour a spoonful of velouté into the rest of your forcemeat and mix well.
Spread this on your plat and place it briefly on the fire.
Arrange your ten quail on it and cover them with lard fat.
A good half hour before serving, put them on a grate with a hot fire underneath.
Cover them with a hot field oven.
At the moment of serving, remove the fat and sauce them with an Italian sauce.
If you have a large hot oven, they will cook even better.
You can also put them au gratin without boning them.

title: Cailles aux Truffes (Quail with Truffles)
description: Prepared with quail, truffles, and lard.
steps: Clean your quail through the cavity and singe them lightly.
Peel your truffles and cut them into large dice.
Grate a little lard and put it in a saucepan with as much butter, salt, pepper, four spices, and a little parsley.
Chop a truffle and mix it with the rest.
Pass this over the fire for seven or eight minutes and let it cool.
Fill the body of your quail with this mixture.
When well filled, truss and bard them and give them an agreeable shape.
Put lard fat in a saucepan with your quail on top and cover them with lard fat.
Cut small pieces of veal into dice, a carrot, seven or eight small onions, a clove, and half a bay leaf.
Add your truffle peelings and a piece of butter.
Put all this in a saucepan and cook your seasoning for a good quarter hour over a moderate fire.
When your seasoning is well browned, add a glass of white wine and as much bouillon.
Let it come to a boil two or three times, then pour this seasoning over your quail when you put them on the fire.
A good half hour is sufficient to cook them.
At the moment of serving, drain them, unbard them, and arrange them on the plate.
In the middle, put a sauté of truffles arranged in a reduced Spanish sauce.

title: Cailles en Gratin (Quail Gratin)
description: Prepared with quail, chives, and bay leaf.
steps: Flame and clean six or seven quail, pass them in a saucepan over the fire with a piece of butter, a bouquet of parsley, chives, half a clove of garlic, two cloves, half a bay leaf, thyme, basil, and mushrooms.
Add a good pinch of flour, moisten with white wine, bouillon, and juice as needed to give color, salt, and coarse pepper.
At half the cooking time, add a sweetbread of veal blanched and cut into large dice, finish cooking and reduce the sauce to the point of a bound sauce.
For the gratin: chop the quail livers with parsley and chives, mix with a little breadcrumbs, a piece of butter, salt, coarse pepper, and two egg yolks.
Place this forcemeat in the bottom of the serving dish and put it over a small fire until the forcemeat is gratinéed.
Serve the ragout over it.

title: Calf's Brains in Aspic (Cervelles de Veau en aspic)
description: Prepared with aspic and calf's brains.
steps: Prepare and cook your brains as you would for the panfried version
Pour lukewarm aspic into the bottom of a mold to a depth of seven or eight lines
When your aspic is cold and set, cut your brains into four pieces and arrange them so that they form a beautiful pattern and are positioned on your jelly to create a design
Pour nearly cold aspic over them so that your brains are well enclosed in the jelly
Place your mold on ice to allow the aspic to congeal

When it is well set, at the moment of serving, heat a cloth well and rub the mold with it until you see your aspic begin to release, or dip the mold in lukewarm water without leaving it in too long for fear the jelly will melt too much
Place your platter over your mold and invert it
If your aspic does not release, place a warm cloth on your mold and rub it around with this same warm cloth
Lift your mold very gently, taking care not to damage your aspic
If there is melted jelly on the platter, use a straw to suck it up
Place your platter briefly on ice

description: Prepared with calf's head, calf's brains, and veal.

ingredients.name: calf's head with skin, well blanched and scalded

steps: Use a calf's head with skin that is well blanched and well scalded.
Carefully remove the skin without cutting it.
Bone the head to extract the brains, tongue, eyes, and cheeks.
Make a forcemeat with the brains, veal round, and beef fat, all chopped very fine.
Season with salt, coarse pepper, parsley, chives (chopped), half a bay leaf, thyme and basil (chopped like powder).
Add two spoonfuls of eau-de-vie and bind the forcemeat with three egg yolks and three beaten egg whites.
Blanch the tongue, eyes (from which you remove all the dark part), and cheeks in boiling water, clean them properly, then cut them into fillets or large dice.
Mix these pieces into your forcemeat.
Place the calf's head skin, unblanced, in a casserole with the ears underneath, and fill it with your forcemeat.
Sew the head closed.

title: Calf's Shoulder in Galantine (Epaule de Veau en galantine)
description: Prepared with meat, lard, and bacon.

ingredients.name: Meat from the shoulder for farce
ingredients.sourceText: Meat from the shoulder for farce

ingredients.name: Lard, one pound for each pound of meat
ingredients.sourceText: Lard, one pound for each pound of meat

ingredients.name: Vegetables and aromatics for the braising liquid: veal slices, two veal feet blanched, shoulder bones, six carrots, eight to ten onions (one studded with four cloves), four bay leaves, thyme, parsley and chives
ingredients.sourceText: Vegetables and aromatics for the braising liquid: veal slices, two veal feet blanched, shoulder bones, six carrots, eight to ten onions (one studded with four cloves), four bay leaves, thyme, parsley and chives

ingredients.name: Beef broth or water and salt
ingredients.sourceText: Beef broth or water and salt

steps: Select a calf's shoulder that is well covered; the top should not be damaged
Bone it entirely
Remove some of the meat with which you will make your farce, if you do not have a slice of veal
For every pound of meat, add a pound of lard that you will chop; when your farce is well chopped, spread it to a thickness of one inch on your shoulder
Lay lardons and pieces of scarlet tongue, truffes if you have them; some people add an omelette made with spinach green, and if you wish, carrots also cut into lardons
To marble your galantine, cover all these ingredients with farce, and add more lardons, truffes, etc., then another layer of farce
When you have used it all, roll your shoulder lengthwise; join your flesh well together; tie it and cover it with lard
Wrap it tightly in canvas or a clean white cloth; tie it once more so that as it cooks it maintains a beautiful form

Place it in a braising pan where you have laid some slices of lard, some slices of veal, two blanched veal feet, the bones from your shoulder, six carrots, eight or ten onions, one of which is studded with four cloves, four bay leaves, a little thyme, a large bouquet of parsley and chives
Moisten with beef broth; if you do not have it, use water and salt
Bring your cooking liquid to boil and braise for three hours; test with a skewer to determine doneness

title: Calf's Tails in Terrine (Queues de veau en terrine)
description: Prepared with beef, mushrooms, and veal.
steps: Cut your tails at the joints; only the section from the thick end to the middle of the tail yields four or five pieces
Sauté them in a good piece of butter without letting them brown, as this ragout must be white
When your meat is well browned in the butter, add four spoonfuls of flour and blend it with your butter and tail
Then add four spoonfuls of consommé
Stir your ragout until it boils; take care to skim it well
Add a portion of turned mushrooms, a bouquet of parsley and chives
Cook your ragout and degrease it when it is three-quarters cooked
When your ragout is completely cooked, remove the pieces of tail with a slotted spoon, along with your mushrooms, and place them in another saucepan
Pour one spoonful of velouté into the sauce of your tails
Reduce this sauce; when you see it is sufficiently reduced and well thickened, strain it through a sieve
Poach veal quenelles in your ragout; drain them at the moment of serving and place them in your terrine
Mix in small pieces of veal shoulder and pieces of veal sweetbreads that you have sautéed in butter; drain them when cooked and place them in your terrine
Add to your tail ragout a liaison of five egg yolks
Stir it gently on the stove until your ragout is thickened; be careful it does not boil for fear it will curdle
Pour it into your terrine over your garnishes, which you will have kept warm; the sauce of your ragout must be abundant so that all the garnishes are bathed in it

title: Canard au Père Douillet (Duck Father Douillet)
description: Prepared with duck, chives, and bay leaf.
steps: Singe and clean the duck well; empty it and truss the legs in a pan just to its size.

Add a bouquet of parsley, chives, one clove of garlic, two cloves, thyme, bay leaf, basil, a good pinch of coriander, onion slices, one carrot, one parsnip, a piece of butter, two glasses of bouillon, and one glass of white wine.
Cook over low heat; when the duck yields under your finger, pass the sauce through a sieve and degrease it.
Reduce the sauce over the fire to the consistency of a sauce.
Serve under the duck.
You can also serve it the same way by cutting it into four pieces before cooking.

title: Canard aux Navets (Duck with Turnips)
description: Prepared with duck, turnips, and bouillon.
steps: Singe the duck; clean, empty, and truss the legs inside.
Put a little butter in a pan with a spoonful of flour; brown it to a nice color and moisten with bouillon.
Put the duck in with a bouquet garni, a little salt, and coarse pepper.
Have turnips properly cut, which you cook with the duck: if they are hard, cook everything at the same time; if they are not, add them halfway through the duck's cooking.
When your ragout is well cooked and degreased, add a little coulis.
Serve short sauce. This is the way to make duck with turnips in the homestyle fashion.

The other way is to cook the duck separately in a white braise, and prepare the turnips turned into ovals, blanched and cooked with bouillon, veal jus and coulis; when your ragout is made, serve it over the duck.

title: Canard aux Olives (Duck with Olives)
description: Prepared with duck, olives, and sauce.
steps: Truss and cook your duck as you would cook duck in a pan
Turn your olives, that is to say remove the flesh from the pit in a corkscrew manner
Keep them whole so they resume their original form
If you wish, let them boil in water, or put them in a saucepan
Put in four spoonfuls of Spanish sauce (espagnole), twice as much consommé or bouillon, a little coarse pepper
Cook your olives on a hot fire; when the sauce is reduced to one third, remove them from the fire
Keep them warm in a bain-marie
If you have no sauce, make a light roux, which you will moisten with the cooking liquid from your duck
Pass it through a silk sieve
If your sauce is not thick enough, add bouillon
At the moment of serving, drain your duck, remove the trussing string, arrange it on your plate, and put your ragout of olives underneath

title: Canard Farci (Stuffed Duck)
description: Prepared with duck, forcemeat, and veal.

ingredients.name: veal round the size of an egg

ingredients.name: beef fat twice the amount of veal
ingredients.sourceText: beef fat twice the amount of veal

steps: Singe and clean the duck through the vent, and bone it entirely without piercing the skin.
Begin deboning from the vent, turning it inside out as you remove the bones.
Fill it halfway with poultry forcemeat or godiveau.

To make godiveau forcemeat: take veal round the size of an egg and twice as much beef fat, chop them together; add parsley, chives, and mushrooms all chopped, two raw eggs, salt, pepper, and half a setier of cream; mix well together and place in the body of the duck.
Tie it up so nothing escapes.
Cook it in a braise like beef tongue (page 29).
When cooked, wipe off the fat and serve with a good sauce or a ragout of chestnuts.
For the chestnut ragout: cook chestnuts with half a setier of white wine, a little coulis, and a pinch of salt, and serve as you see fit.

Half an hour before serving, put them on the grill on a gentle fire

description: Prepared with bouillon, onions, and water.
steps: Cut them to the length of three inches, do not use those that are hollow and green

The sauce should be neither too clear nor too thick, and of a beautiful blonde color
If you wish to serve them in the lean way, put them in a sauce as is said for chard with leeks

Pour the onions and their sauce into the casserole with the prepared fish and season with salt, pepper, and a bouquet garni of fine herbs.
Cook the matelote over high heat for half an hour.
When ready to serve, add some bread croutons to the sauce and serve with the matelote.

Arrange around it carp quenelles or pigeons à la Gautier, glazed veal sweetbreads, glazed veal knuckles, crayfish, poultry foie gras, truffles, rooster crests and kidneys
If the cooking liquid is not too seasoned, pass it through silk sieve
In a saucepan put two spoonfuls of espagnole and two spoonfuls of the carp cooking liquid
Reduce the sauce by half
Add the small garnishes and pour the sauce around the carp after glazing it

title: Carré de Mouton en Crépine (Lamb Square in Caul)
description: Prepared with lamb, onions, and bouillon.
steps: Cut into slices about ten or fifteen onions, depending on their size.
Pass them on the fire with a piece of butter, stirring often with a spoon, until they are completely cooked.
Cut a lamb square into cutlets and cook them on low heat with bouillon, a little salt, and coarse pepper.
When they are cooked, reduce the sauce until it clings entirely to the cutlets and remove them on a plate.
Drain the fat in the saucepan and put half a glass of bouillon in the same saucepan to detach what sticks to it.
Pass this small sauce through a sieve to mix with the onions and three egg yolks.
Bind them on the fire without boiling, for fear they turn.
Take caul that you have soaked in water; press it well to divide it into as many pieces as you have cutlets.
Put on each piece of caul one cutlet with the onion all around the cutlet; wrap everything with caul and seal all the edges with beaten egg.
Then dip them everywhere in beaten egg to coat them with bread crumbs.
Arrange them on a plate that can go in the fire.
Baste all the top with good fat or olive oil.
Put them in the oven or under a pastry lid cover until they have taken on a beautiful golden color and remove them on a cloth to drain them of their fat.
Serve with a sauce made as follows: Put in a saucepan half a glass of white wine, as much bouillon, a little jus, salt, and coarse pepper.
Boil and reduce by half; serve under the cutlets.

title: Carré de Mouton à la Conti (Lamb Square Conti Style)
description: Prepared with lamb, bacon, and anchovies.
steps: Prepare a lamb square by removing the skins found on the filet.

Take a quarter pound of well-larded bacon and two washed anchovies; cut them into larding strips and mix with a little coarse pepper, two shallots, parsley, and chives, all chopped, half a bay leaf, three or four basil leaves chopped like powder, and three or four tarragon leaves also chopped.
Lard the entire filet with the bacon and anchovies.
Put the square with all these fine herbs in a saucepan.
Moisten with one glass of white wine and an equal amount of bouillon.
Cook on low heat.
When it is cooked, degrease the sauce and add a knob of butter the size of a walnut mixed with a pinch of flour.
Bind the sauce on the fire and serve it over the lamb square.
