title: Carré de Veau Piqué Glacé aux Concombres (Larded Glazed Veal Square with Cucumbers)
description: Prepared with veal, lard, and carrots.

ingredients.name: Whole square of veal from the rib near the kidney to the second rib near the collar
ingredients.sourceText: Whole square of veal from the rib near the kidney to the second rib near the collar

steps: Take a whole square of veal from the rib near the kidney to the second rib near the collar.
Trim and cut it as squarely as possible.
Remove the bones that are under the fillet to the end of the rib of the chapelet.
Uncover the fillet, that is to say lift the skins that cover it.
Remove the nerves that are on it by introducing your knife between the nerve and the flesh, so that your fillet is well uncovered and no skin remains on it.
Then lard it with fine lard.
Fasten the skins covering the ribs with a trussing needle and string.

When your square is larded and trussed, place strips of lard in a small braising pan, slices of veal, two or three carrots, four onions, two laurel leaves, a bouquet of parsley and chives, two cloves.
Place your square over this seasoning so that your larded fillet can receive the heat of the fire on top of your braising pan.
Cover the skins covering the ribs with strips of lard.
Have a sheet of paper folded in double and buttered, which you place on your square.
Add two spoonfuls of consommé or bouillon.
Add a little salt.
Cook on low heat for three hours.
Be careful to put fire on top of the lid to glaze your fillet.
At the moment of serving, drain your square and untie it, that is to say remove the string.

description: Prepared with veal, lard, and chives.
steps: Cut the half pound of lard into lardons and mix them with parsley, ciboule, a small clove of garlic, all chopped, a bay leaf, thyme, and basil chopped to a powder, salt, and coarse pepper
Lard with this mixture the fillet of a veal square, after having cut the bones at the bottom of the fillet

description: Prepared with veal, chives, and mushrooms.

ingredients.name: butter kneaded with a pinch of flour
ingredients.sourceText: butter kneaded with a pinch of flour

steps: Lard the entire fillet of a veal square after having trimmed it properly

Place it in a terrine to marinate for three hours with parsley, ciboule, a bit of fennel, mushrooms, a bay leaf, thyme, basil, two shallots, all chopped very fine, salt, coarse pepper, grated nutmeg, and a bit of oil
When it has taken on flavor, spit the square, put all its seasoning on top, and wrap it in two sheets of white paper well buttered
Tie it so that the small herbs cannot escape, and cook it over a small fire

When cooking is done, remove the paper and scrape off with a knife all the small herbs that cling to the paper and the meat, to put them in a saucepan with a bit of juice, two spoonfuls of verjuice, butter kneaded with a pinch of flour, a bit of salt, and coarse pepper
Make the sauce bind over the fire to serve under the square

Before binding the sauce, melt a bit of butter and mix in an egg yolk to rub on top of the square and bread it with breadcrumbs, and brown it nicely; you can also serve it without being breaded if you are indifferent about appearance

Reserve some false Béchamel in which you put a piece of glace about the size of a walnut, a little coarse pepper, a little nutmeg
Pour this sauce underneath; it should not be too thick

title: Chartreuse de Pommes (Apple Chartreuse)
description: Prepared with apples, lemon, and lemon juice.
steps: Remove the peel from several apples
Put water in a terrine with three lemon juices
Use a small tin mold to cut your apples into small sticks
Put them in the water, and the rest of the apples as well, so they do not blacken
Clarify three quarterons of sugar in which you press the juice of one lemon
Put the small sticks in it
Let them boil once or twice, they should only be softened
Remove them from the sugar and drain them on a sieve
Cut the apple scraps into small slices and put them in the sugar
When softened, remove them or let them reduce to marmalade
Arrange symmetrically the small apple sticks around a lightly buttered mold
Place some in the bottom
Put apple marmalade on top, apricot marmalade inside
The mold must be full so it can be unmolded and your chartreuse holds together without the decoration falling apart
You can add candied cherries, verjuice, basil, citron peel, etc. for decoration
If you do not use a mold, put a mass of marmalade on a plate, give it a round or square shape, arrange the apple sticks and candied fruits with symmetry
You can reduce the syrup, put it on a plate, when it is set, you can use it to mask your chartreuse

sourceSteps: Remove the peel from several apples
Put water in a terrine with three lemon juices
Use a small tin mold to cut your apples into small sticks

You can reduce the syrup, put it on a plate, when it is set, you can use it to mask your chartreuse

title: Chicorée au Velouté (Chicory in Velvet Sauce)
description: A sauce made with velouté, consommé, and salt.
steps: Remove the outer part of the chicory so that only the white remains
Cut the head and place the chicory split in two in water to wash
Have a pot of boiling water with a handful of salt; place the chicory in it
Push it down in the water from time to time so it does not blacken
When you see it mixes with the water, it is sufficiently blanched
Test with your fingers; if it is soft, drain it in a colander and place it in fresh water
When well cooled, drain it again and squeeze it in your hands to extract the water
Then chop it
Put a good piece of butter in a pot with the chicory, a little salt, and coarse pepper
Stir it often and pour five tablespoons of velouté sauce and the same of consommé over it
Let it reduce until somewhat thick
Then arrange it on the platter with croutons around it

title: Chicorée Braisée (Braised Chicory)
description: Prepared with velouté, consommé, and butter.
steps: If the chicory yields when pressed, drain it in a colander and place it in fresh water; when well chilled, drain it again and press it in your hands to extract the water.
Chop the chicory.

Put a good piece of butter in a saucepan with the chicory, a little salt, and coarse pepper; stir it much and pour over it about five tablespoons of velouté and as much consommé; reduce it until it becomes somewhat thick.
Dress it on the plate with croutons around it.
If you wish to make chicory with cream or bouillon, add about two teaspoons of flour and moisten the chicory with cream or bouillon; if you have added too much liquid, reduce it.

title: Chicorée Conservée pour l'Hiver (Preserved Chicory for Winter)
description: Prepared with clarified butter, salt, and water.
steps: Toward the end of September, take one hundred heads of chicory or more
Remove the hard green ribs that envelop the white part, keeping only the good parts
Rinse the head without cutting too close
Have a large cauldron three-quarters full of boiling water
Put two large handfuls of salt in the water
When the water boils, add your chicory, well-washed and drained
Be careful to submerge it in the boiling water so it does not blacken
After it has boiled for ten minutes, remove it and put it in cold water
When well refreshed, remove it and press it in your hands to extract the water
Arrange it in jars or pots
Make a brine
When it is cold and clear, pour it over your chicory
Cover it with clarified butter
When it is congealed, close your container

title: Choux Farcis (Stuffed Cabbage)
description: Prepared with veal, pork fat, and egg yolks.
steps: Blanch two medium cabbages in water and salt; when they have been twenty minutes in boiling water, refresh them and let them drain; remove the hearts.

Chop half a pound of veal; add one pound of pork fat, salt, coarse pepper, a little four-spice, and a little crushed aromatics; when all is well chopped, add seven or eight egg yolks that you will mix well with your stuffing.
Put the stuffing inside each cabbage; tie them well.
Arrange lard strips in the bottom of a saucepan, some veal slices, a little ham, three carrots, four onions, a little thyme, a bay leaf, two cloves; put the cabbages on top and cover them with lard.
Moisten them with bouillon from the bottom of the pot; add a little salt and pepper; let them simmer for an hour and a half.

When they are cooked, drain them on white cloth; extract the juice by pressing them a little; then untie them and give them an agreeable shape; you can dress them on the plate; glaze them and put Spanish sauce underneath; if you have no sauce, make a light roux, moisten it with the cooking liquid, and pass it through silk strainer.

Spread a good meat farce seasoned to taste over it, approximately the thickness of a large coin
On this farce place a row of ham lardons, then a row of lard, then a row of truffles, then a row of hard egg yolks
Cover all these lardons with a bit more farce

Wrap it in lard barding and cheesecloth
Tie it tightly with string
Cook for three hours with half bouillon and half white wine, salt, coarse pepper, turnips, onions, a large bouquet of parsley, chives, shallots, garlic, cloves, thyme, bay leaf, and basil
Allow it to cool in its cooking liquid
Serve cold as an entremets

title: Cochon de Lait par Quartier au Père Douillet (Suckling Pig Quarters Père Douillet Style)
description: Prepared with suckling pig, beef, and veal.
steps: Make a good broth with beef brisket, veal knuckle and two feet, a bouquet of parsley, chives, two garlic cloves, three cloves, half a nutmeg, onions, and roots
Once the meat is cooked, strain the broth through a sieve
Put the suckling pig in a vessel proportioned to its size, with four large crayfish and the strained broth

Strain the cooking liquid through a sieve and degrease it, then put it on a stove to clarify it like a jelly by adding half a lemon with skin removed and six egg whites beaten with the shells

Put the suckling pig in a vessel just its size, with the four crayfish underneath and branches of parsley
